images.title: A safe pair of numbers
images.purpose: Show that 4 and 9 are a safe pair because their only common factor is 1.
images.composition: Two number cards side by side with wide space, and one line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: number 4 in a teal #0072B2 box with its factors 1, 2, 4 below. Right: number 9 in an amber #E69F00 box with its factors 1, 3, 9 below. Below, centred: one line. Exactly 2 boxes, 6 factors in total.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any extra shared factor drawn between the two cards
images.takeaway: A safe pair has no common factor except 1.
images.description: Number 4 in teal with factors 1, 2, 4 and number 9 in amber with factors 1, 3, 9; the only common factor is 1.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to look for a factor that both cards share.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
